title: The binary tape head read preserves its exact representation
author: @marwahaha
source: The proof follows the three possible head cases. For a blank stack the pop instruction enters the blank state. For an explicit bit it pops that bit, then pushes the same bit back and enters its distinct return state. Each instruction increments the bit-operation counter once and none changes oracle calls.

title: Combined survivor minimum honours statutory anti-franking
author: @WillR
source: Original derived statutory UK DB benefit contracts based on Pension Schemes Act 1993 sections 87–92 (including statutory relevant sum, appropriate addition, later earnings addition and exclusions), https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/part/IV/chapter/III; and Pensions Act 1995 section 53 (next-year above-statutory credit and full deemed increase), https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/26/section/53. Historic cessation-date definitions and GMP age, s88 pension-at-cessation or short service benefits, s89 additional accrual and postponement enhancements, and the s90(3) assumed earnings/GMP inputs must be certified member-by-member. The ordinary member/survivor branches exclude complete substituted benefits requiring alternative s87(3)(a) treatment, and do not by themselves implement all of sections 87–92, section 91 special service rules or s92 commutation disregard. Monetary inputs are weekly unless explicitly converted, and section 53 credits are already certified amounts.

title: The register program reads the decoded tape head
author: @marwahaha
source: Split on the finite right stack. An empty stack takes the blank branch; a nonempty stack reads its head, restores the popped bit, and enters the branch encoding that symbol. The head-relative decoder and both stack registers are therefore unchanged.

title: A fixed machine moves its binary tape head left exactly
author: @marwahaha
source: The machine pops the old current cell and then the previous left cell. The control state retains both bits while two pushes prepend the old current cell and then the new current cell to the right stack. Empty stacks supply false, so the same four instructions handle missing cells.

author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

source: Source-faithful child for AvramDividend.Classical.barrier_zero_boundary_value (9e8e88ea-7f12-4d95-a4d1-a54abfee9305), pinned at Mathlib revision 0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474. The real-cutoff Fourier/mesh source already constructs the dyadic negative bump sequence and proves smoothness, compact support, range [0,1], vanishing near zero, integrability, and divergence of its restricted Levy integrals (candidates/work_on/AvramDividend_Classical_barrier_zero_boundary_value_9e8e88ea_fourier_partition_20261028.lean, lines 3451-4080). This isolates a genuine analytic step used to turn infinite negative activity into mesh hit-rate lower bounds. The child depends only on X and its Levy measure; it does not depend on the parent theorem, so it creates no cycle. The publication declares a new Open problem only: no parent-child edge or proof of barrier_zero_boundary_value is claimed, and the formal bridge remains to be established through the early-jump mesh argument.

title: Qualifying survivor statutory GMP minimum
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: Gaussian damped primitive bounds yield local geometric bounds for undamped Neumann terms
author: @WillR
source: Define the undamped Neumann term Q0=1/a and Q_{n+1}(s)=exp(w s) H_n(s). On any interval Ioc(0,x), 0≤w and s≤x imply exp(w s)≤exp(w x). The proved bound |H_n(s)|≤ρ^(n+1)/a then yields |Q_n(s)|≤C_x ρ^n for C_x=max(1/a,exp(w x)/a). This supplies precisely hQ to causal_geometric_neumann_local_sum_bound and then causal_local_neumann_convolution_majorant.

author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: A fibrewise-normalised time-dependent likelihood preserves the observation-clock distribution exactly
author: @WillR
source: Use measure extensionality on measurable sets B of ℝ. Expand `Measure.map Prod.snd` and `withDensity_apply`, rewrite the restricted joint density integral as an indicator integral, and apply `lintegral_prod_symm` to integrate first over paths P. The indicator of {t∈B} factors through the second coordinate, so fibrewise normalisation yields `B.indicator 1` integrated over η. Pinned `lintegral_indicator_const` evaluates this as η(B). All equalities hold for the true weighted product measure, not an assumed infinite-time tilted process.

source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: GMP revaluation is a different operation
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. title: An actual time-dependent finite-rate Esscher law retains its external exponential observation-time marginal
author: @WillR
source: Under the original Lévy probability structure X.isProbability and Mathlib's positive-rate exponential distribution, apply the accepted `chat04_fibrewise_normalized_joint_tilt_clock_marginal` to the concrete Esscher density. For every real observation time t, its nonnegative clamp Real.toNNReal t has an accepted finite-horizon tilted probability law; its total mass rewritten via `withDensity_apply` and `Measure.restrict_univ` is 1, exactly the generic theorem's fibrewise normalisation. This proves equality of measures without any tilted infinite-horizon path law.

author: @WillR

Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: Sharp real three-dimensional Hlawka bound for 535/32 <= p <= 1071/64
author: @shivm
source: Original cutoff-16 extension, 25 October 2026, complete window 13. Extends Sections 3-5 of Yuxuan Xu, A computer-assisted sharp diagonal Hlawka inequality for real exponents p >= 21, https://github.com/Anchen-AI4Math/hlawka-diagonal-certificates/blob/2f1ec21c8ce4e3d9de33f57119f73f8504de0bd3/paper/main.tex . title: Statutory member floor retains unchanged pre-88 part
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: Revaluation at GMP commencement distinct from increases
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: No 6 April GMP increase before GMP becomes payable
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: Independent exponential observation time and underlying random path coordinates
author: @WillR
source: Mathlib already provides `ProbabilityTheory.indepFun_prod` for two measurable functions of disjoint coordinates of a product measure. Instantiate both functions as identity maps, with μ=P and ν=ProbabilityTheory.expMeasure p, applying `measurable_id` twice. The resulting independence is an authentic probabilistic property of the constructed product law, not a formal postulate or an assumption about the existence of a global Esscher process.

title: Finite-grid downward-barrier crossing probability has a uniform exponential Esscher bound
author: @WillR
source: By the proved Lévy exponent secant monotonicity, ψ(φ/2)≤q/2, so the compensated Esscher exponential drift κ=ψφ−ψ(φ/2)≥0. A crossing at index k implies its exponential martingale is at least exp(φb/2), and hence so is the finite-grid maximum. Use Finset.le_sup' for the sampled index, measure monotonicity, and the already Proved `chat04_esscher_leftshift_terminal_grid_doob_maximal_bound` under Q_T. The proof requires neither a global tilted probability nor Wiener–Hopf and is the critical input for passing to dense continuous-time grids.

title: Nil statutory pre-88 GMP increase
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: October GPD to 6 April earns full three per cent
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: Distinct rational markings after a finite field extension
author: @tomasz
source: Auxiliary finite-generic-point marking step for A. J. de Jong, Smoothness, semi-stability and alterations, Publications Mathématiques de l’IHÉS 83 (1996), Section 4.16-4.17, pp. 71-72, https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1996__83__51_0.pdf . This is a derived and generalized field-valued marking statement, not the full family or componentwise marking theorem of Section 5.2. Closed-point residue fields are finite by the Hilbert Nullstellensatz, as in Stacks Project Lemma 29.21.3, tag 01TF, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01TF . The proof takes a finite compositum of their embeddings in an algebraic closure and uses actual cartesian lifts. It does not assert separability or stable reduction.

title: Joint Borel measurability of right-continuous processes with measurable deterministic-time sections
author: @WillR
source: Approximate each observation time t≥0 from above by dyadic ceilings r_n(t)=Nat.ceil(t2^n)/2^n. Pinned Prove2Me theorems prove r_n(t)≥t and r_n(t)→t. For each n, map z=(t,ω) to the measurable integer ceil(t2^n), and use Mathlib `exists_measurable_piecewise` to glue each measurable finite-grid sample F_(k/2^n) along the disjoint observable fibres k. Thus z↦F_(r_n(t))(ω) is jointly measurable. Right-continuity yields convergence via tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff. Mathlib measurable_of_tendsto_metrizable and tendsto_pi_nhds conclude the result. This is self-contained in the exact pinned environment, and does not depend on any unverified project helper.

title: Finite-horizon Esscher exponential tilt defines an actual probability measure
author: @WillR
source: Use Proved esscher_exp_process_integrable and levy_compensated_exponential_expectation_one. The exponential density is nonnegative, so Mathlib ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal identifies its ENNReal mass with one; `withDensity_apply` gives measure_univ=1. This is the fundamental construction for proving that finite-horizon Esscher survival masses are genuine CDFs of the reflected running infimum and can be assembled via the Stieltjes machinery.
